recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The requested clarification is already present in the active RESTful API source; future changes should only be made under a new work-group decision reopening the broader HTTP Location header rules.
issue_request: FHIR-13915 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core HTTP issue asking how a create response Location header should be formed when a server does not support version-specific retrieval. The approved resolution was to document that Location should be as specific as the server can supply: include the version when the server understands versioning, and allow [base]/[type]/[id] when it does not.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 14043. The corresponding git-svn commit fa063a9991eb8c08d9ca71ed51016822812eb338 changed source/http.html to add the as-specific-as-possible Location wording and the explicit [base]/[type]/[id] fallback for servers that do not track versions.
additional_context: The active source remains source/http.html for the FHIR-core RESTful API page. Later FHIR-17746 added that Location MAY be absolute or relative in the same paragraph, and later FHIR-26358 and FHIR-31965 addressed Location-header behavior for update and conditional create/update without reversing the FHIR-13915 fallback. A 2022 Zulip thread quoted the current create Location rule as clear guidance, and direct FHIR-13915 Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. Current source/http.html says create responses use Location: [base]/[type]/[id]/_history/[vid] when versioning is available, then explicitly says servers that do not track versions use [base]/[type]/[id]. Neighboring update and conditional-create text points back to the same create behavior and does not require a separate FHIR-13915 correction.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue clarified in the same Location paragraph that absolute and relative URLs are both allowed.
Later Published issue extended mandatory Location header handling to update and conditional create/update while preserving the FHIR-13915 version fallback.
Later Published conditional-create issue expected Location, ETag, and Last-Modified headers to align with ordinary create behavior.
